scope: Prospective source-role probe and specificity design, training/split/threshold semantics, analysis code review; not final output verification
reviewed_properties: Whole-world splits preserve all conditions/agents, with heldout families.
Role, configured condition, individual behavior, and paired submission labels are separate.
Paired unauthorized submission now depends on exactly two observed actor target actions and absent authorization, irrespective of team metadata.
Source StandardScaler fit on source training discussion states only; fixed C25 and layer28 Peak primary;8iterations and2000 sensitivity both retained.
Source final all-honest calibration threshold uses six calibration worlds, never test outcomes;90/95/100th sensitivity disclosed.
Pooled actual-action flag rates use world-cluster intervals and count distinct worlds; invalid actor optimistic bounds retained.
Failed attempts and invalid responses are not filtered from assigned-condition denominators; incomplete four-agent groups explicitly omitted only where group statistics undefined.
resolved_review_findings: Removed team-metadata gate from actual paired-action label.
Changed pooled multiple-condition uncertainty to world clusters.
Added invalid-actor identification bounds and source-context/calibration limitations.
remaining_limits: Six calibration worlds cannot certify a population5%FPR.
Source final prompts omit private exchange except public-discussion consequences; short public round/BF16/prospective boundary are adaptations.
Two actors independently selecting target is paired unauthorized submission, not successful collusion or an executed joint operation.
A role-trained probe can decode instructions/persona; detecting assigned colluders does not establish prediction of naturally occurring unauthorized behavior.
If actual unauthorized examples are absent, no behavior sensitivity can be estimated; an AUROC from configuration labels must not substitute.
recommendation: Collection/analysis may proceed after root pilot gate. Final conclusions must distinguish source role discrimination, new-task false positives and actual-action prediction.
